title: Imperfecto vs Indefinido — The Core Contrast

sections.content: You know both simple past tenses: the indefinido from Unit 11 and the imperfecto from Unit 21. This unit shows how to choose between them. The pretérito imperfecto describes the background — ongoing situations, habits, and states. The pretérito indefinido (also called pretérito perfecto simple) narrates specific completed events that advanced the story.

items.spanish: Llovía mucho cuando llegué a casa.
items.english: It was raining a lot when I arrived home.

items.spanish: Hacía frío, pero salimos de todas formas.
items.english: It was cold, but we went out anyway.

items.spanish: Caminaba por la calle cuando vi a María.
items.english: I was walking down the street when I saw María.

sections.content: A useful test: if you can say 'was/were doing' in English, use the imperfecto. If you can say 'did' (a single, completed action), use the indefinido.

Signals for IMPERFECTO: siempre, normalmente, cada día, cuando era niño.
Signals for INDEFINIDO: ayer, el lunes, de repente (for the new event), entonces, por fin, una vez.
